1     GENERAL PLANT AND SITE DESCRIPTION AND OVERVIEW OF LICENSING
      BASIS
1.1       Introduction

This safety evaluation (SE) documents the results of the U.S Nuclear Regulatory Commission
(NRC) staff’s (staff) technical review of the construction permit (CP) application submitted by
Long Mott Energy, LLC (LME) for the Long Mott Generating Station (LMGS). The LMGS CP
application was submitted under Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations, Part 50 (10 CFR
50) by letter dated March 31, 2025 (ML25090A057) and proposes to construct an 800
megawatt-thermal (MWth) nuclear power plant comprising four X Energy, LLC (X-energy) Xe-
100 small modular high-temperature gas-cooled reactors (HTGRs) and associated common
facilities in Calhoun County, Texas. The CP application consists of the following parts:

      •    Part I – General and Financial Information
      •    Part II – Preliminary Safety Analysis Report
      •    Part III – Environmental Report
      •    Part IV – Technical Specifications
      •    Part V – Non-Applicabilities and Exemptions
      •    Part VI – Supplemental Information
      •    Part VII – Security-Related Information to be Withheld per 10 CFR 2.390(d)(1)

The staff published notices in the Federal Register (FR) on May 2, May 9, May 16, and May 23,
2025 (90 FR 18874, 90 FR 19733, 90 FR 21080, and 90 FR 22118 to acknowledge receipt of
LME’s CP application. The staff conducted an acceptance review for docketing of LME’s LMGS
CP application and, by letter dated May 12, 2025 (ML25115A247) determined that LME’s LMGS
CP application was complete and acceptable for docketing. The application was assigned
Docket Number (No.) 50-614. A notice of docketing of LME’s LMGS CP application was
published in the FR on June 10, 2025 (90 FR 24428).

The staff’s SE of the CP application to construct the 10 CFR Part 50 utilization facility is based
on information in revision 1 of the CP application which was submitted on September 18, 2026
(ML26261A419), and responses to requests for confirmation of information (ML26239A157 and
ML26260C204). Revision 1 of the CP application incorporated the following supplements to the
initial application submitted on March 31, 2025 (ML25090A057) associated with the safety
review:

The LMP guidance in NEI 18-04 defines risk-informed, performance-based, and technology-
inclusive processes for the selection of licensing basis events (LBEs); safety classification of
SSCs; and the determination of defense-in-depth (DID) adequacy for non-light-water reactors
(non-LWRs). NEI 18-04 provides a frequency-consequence target curve that is used to assess
events, SSCs, and programmatic controls. LBEs are categorized by the frequency of
occurrence, separated into anticipated operational occurrences, design-basis events (DBEs),
and beyond-design-basis events.
Figure 1-1 provides a high-level level flow diagram for the NEI 18-04 process with important
components and results represented along with where they are described in the preliminary
safety analysis report (PSAR). Additional information important to the safety basis that is not
represented in the figure includes the site characteristics that determine the design basis hazard
levels and provide atmospheric dispersion information for the consequence analysis in chapter
2, the evaluation of DID in chapter 4, preliminary discussions on aspects primarily pertaining to
the operating license in chapters 9-12, and the research and development program to address
remaining safety questions prior to the completion of construction in chapter 13.

NEI 21-07, Revision 1 describes guidance on the scope and level of detail for specific portions
of the first eight chapters of a PSAR that are associated with LMP-based safety analysis.
DANU-ISG-2022-01 provides (1) a general overview of the information that should be included
in a non-LWR application submitted under 10 CFR Part 50 or 10 CFR Part 52; (2) a review
roadmap for NRC staff with the principal purpose of ensuring consistency, quality, and
uniformity of the staff reviews; and (3) a well-defined base from which the staff can evaluate
proposed differences in the scope of reviews (e.g., CP versus OL). RGs 1.233 and 1.253 as
well as other key guidance documents are referenced in DANU ISG-2022-01.
As appropriate, the staff used additional guidance and codes and standards (e.g., NRC RGs,
Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers standards, and American National Standards
Institute/American Nuclear Society (ANSI/ANS) standards) in its review of the LMGS CP
application.

The following additional requirements, not directly addressed by the LMGS CP application, are
evaluated as follows:

Nuclear Waste Policy Act

The Nuclear Waste Policy Act of 1982 (42 USC § 10101) provides that the U.S. Government is
responsible for the permanent disposal of high-level radioactive waste and spent nuclear fuel,
but the cost of disposal should be the responsibility of the generators and owners of such waste
and spent fuel. Guidance for the staff to evaluate compliance with the Nuclear Waste Policy Act
is provided in DANU-ISG-2022-01. The applicant’s letter dated March 31, 2025, submitting the
CP application stated that “LME is in good faith negotiations with the U.S. Department of Energy
to enter into a contract for the disposal of high-level waste and nuclear fuel under section 302(b)
of the Nuclear Waste Policy Act of 1982, as amended.” By letter dated October 2, 2026
(ML26275A165), LME provided documentation from DOE that LME is actively and in good faith
negotiating on a contract under section 302(b) of the Nuclear Waste Policy Act. Because LME
has provided documentation of good faith negotiations with the U.S. Department of Energy, the
staff finds that LME is in compliance with the Nuclear Waste Policy Act at the CP stage,
consistent with DANU-ISG-2022-01.

Ongoing Research and Development

The provisions of 10 CFR 50.34(a)(8) allow for ongoing research and development (R&D) to
confirm the adequacy of the design of SSCs to resolve safety questions prior to the completion
of construction. In accordance with 10 CFR 50.34(a)(8), LME identified several R&D activities,
which are described in PSAR chapter 13. Chapter 13 of this SE evaluates these activities.

Advisory Committee on Reactor Safeguards Review

To support the Advisory Committee on Reactor Safeguards (ACRS) in providing an independent
review and report to the Commission regarding the LMGS CP application, the NRC staff
presented the results of its SE to the ACRS subcommittee on September 1 and 2, 2026 and
September 15, 2026 and to the full committee on October 7, 2026. After the meetings, the
ACRS issued a letter to the Commission (MLXXXXX) with their recommendations regarding the

1.2     Summary and Conclusions on Principal Safety Considerations

The staff evaluated the descriptions and discussions of the proposed LMGS facility, as
described in LME’s CP application, as supplemented. Based on its review, the staff makes the
following findings:

      1. Applicable standards and requirements of the Atomic Energy Act and Commission
         regulations have been met.

      2. The application generally conforms to the applicable guidance for a CP applicant for a
         commercial non-LWR, with acceptable departures as noted in this SE.

      3. Required notifications to other agencies or bodies related to this licensing action have
         been duly made.

      4. Based on the preliminary design of the facility, there is reasonable assurance that the
         final design will conform to the design basis with adequate margin for safety.

      5. There is reasonable assurance that the facility can be constructed in conformity with the
         permit, the provisions of the Atomic Energy Act, and the Commission’s regulations.

      6. The staff has evaluated the accident analyses presented by LME in the PSAR and
         determined that the calculated potential radiation dose consequences outside the LMGS
         site from postulated accidents are not likely to exceed the dose guidelines of 10 CFR
         50.34(a)(1)(ii)(D), taking into consideration the site criteria contained in 10 CFR Part


                     OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION
                    OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION


       100. Furthermore, SSCs have been designed to provide for the prevention of accidents
       and the mitigation of consequences of accidents.

   7. Releases of radioactive materials and wastes from the facility are not expected to result
      in concentrations outside the limits specified by 10 CFR Part 20, Subpart D, “Radiation
      Dose Limits for Individual Members of the Public,” and are as low as is reasonably
      achievable.

   8. The financial information, technical analyses, programs, and organization described in
      the application, as supplemented, demonstrate that LME is financially and technically
      qualified to engage in the construction of its proposed facility in accordance with the
      Commission’s regulations.

   9. The preliminary emergency plan provides reasonable assurance that LME will be
      prepared to assess and respond to emergency events.

   10. The application presents information at a level of detail that is appropriate for general
       familiarization and understanding of the proposed facility.

   11. The application describes the relationship of specific facility design features to reactor
       operation.

   12. Issuance of the CP will not be inimical to the common defense and security or to the
       health and safety of the public.

Therefore, the staff finds that, subject to certain conditions, the preliminary design and analysis
of LMGS, as described in the PSAR, is sufficient to meet the applicable regulatory requirements
for the issuance of a CP in accordance with 10 CFR 50.35.

The staff notes that there are some remaining areas of uncertainty in the LMGS design and
analysis, as discussed throughout this SE. This is acceptable under the requirements of 10 CFR
50.34(a) and 10 CFR 50.35, which state that the expected design and analysis is preliminary
and that outstanding safety questions may be resolved through R&D efforts. The staff also
notes that, per 10 CFR 50.35(b), a CP does not constitute Commission approval of any design
feature unless specifically requested and incorporated into the permit; no such approval was
requested in the application. As stated in this SE where applicable, further technical information
or design information required to complete the safety analysis can reasonably be left for later
consideration in the FSAR. LME stated in the PSAR and supplements where they intend to
provide such information at the OL stage of the review. The staff notes that resolution of these
items is not necessary for the issuance of a CP.

In PSAR chapter 13, LME identified several ongoing R&D activities to confirm the adequacy of
the design of SSCs to resolve safety questions prior to the completion of construction. The staff
is tracking these activities and, if an OL application is submitted, will ensure they are
appropriately completed pursuant to 10 CFR 50.34(b)(5). Additionally, appendix X to this SE
identifies certain permit conditions that the staff recommends the Commission include if the CP
is issued, which are intended in part to ensure the staff has access to information on certain
areas where the design and analysis is expected to mature between the CP and OL stages.

Based on these findings as documented in this SE, and subject to the permit conditions
identified in appendix X of this SE, the staff recommends that the Commission make the

following conclusions for the issuance of a CP for the LMGS facility in accordance with 10 CFR

      6. LME is technically qualified to engage in the construction of its proposed facility in

      8. The issuance of a permit for the construction of LMGS would not be inimical to the

      9. After weighing the environmental, economic, technical, and other benefits of the facility

1.3     Plant Description, Site Description, Plant Safety Overview, and Definitions

Chapter 1 of the PSAR contains the following information:

   •   PSAR Section 1.1, “Plant Description,” presents information regarding the reactor and its
       intended use, along with a high-level description of the plant’s structures, systems, and
       components (SSCs).

   •   PSAR Section 1.2, “Site Description,” presents a high-level description of the site
       location.

   •   PSAR Section 1.3, “Plant Safety Overview,” provides a high-level overview of (1) the
       selection of LBEs for the LMGS design, (2) required safety function (RSFs) identified for
       the LMGS design (including fundamental safety functions and additional required safety
       functions), and (3) the guidance used to evaluate defense-in-depth adequacy.

   •   PSAR Section 1.4, “Regulatory Analysis, “contains the assessment of the applicability of
       GSIs, USIs, and TMI action items, identifies the RGs and consensus codes and
       standards applied to the LMGS design, and identifies the licensing topical reports (TRs)
       incorporated by reference into the LMGS PSAR.

   •   PSAR Section 1.5, “Definitions,” contains the list of definitions used in the LMGS PSAR.

PSAR Sections 1.1 through 1.3 and 1.5 are evaluated in this section and are not associated
with specific NRC regulatory requirements, but follow the guidance provided in NEI 21-07, as
endorsed by RG 1.253.
PSAR section 1.1 provides a brief description of the type of reactor being proposed, the
intended use of the reactor, and the overall configuration. The reactor model is the Xe-100 high
temperature gas-cooled reactor (HTGR) supplied by X-energy, LLC. Each reactor is 200
megawatts-thermal (MWt), 80 megawatts-electric (MWe) and is fueled with uranium oxy-carbide
(UCO) tri-structural isotropic (TRISO) coated fuel embedded in spherical fuel elements, referred
to as pebbles. Each Xe-100 reactor core contains approximately 220,000 pebbles and is cooled
by forced circulation of helium through the pebble bed. The heat is transferred from the fuel by
the helium to a steam generator (SG) where it is used to generate superheated steam. The
steam is used to generate electricity and as process steam for the Seadrift Operations (SDO)
site which is adjacent to the proposed LMGS site.

The LMGS plant includes four Xe-100 reactors and SG pairs located on a single nuclear island
(NI) with a shared reactor building foundation and shield structure. Additional systems shared
between reactor modules are listed in PSAR section 1.1.3. The sharing of these systems is
evaluated in chapters 6 and 7 through principal design criterion (PDC) 5. PSAR section 1.1.3
also includes a comparison to similar facilities, including Fort St. Vrain, an 842 MWt HTGR that
previously operated in the United States.

PSAR section 1.1.4 includes a summary description of plant SSCs, including reactor systems
and components, secondary systems and components, significant support systems and
components, and the major structures. Safety-significant SSCs (i.e., those that are assigned a
safety classification of safety-related (SR) or non-safety-related with special treatment (NSRST))
are described in further detail in PSAR chapters 6 and 7 and evaluated in chapters 6 and 7 of
this SE. Liquid radwaste and solid radwaste handling systems (LRWH and SRWH) are
described in more detail in PSAR chapter 9 and evaluated in chapter 9 of this SE. However,

1.3.1   Technical Evaluation

Plant Description

The role of SFFPs and the startup source in the transition from the non-fuel core to the steady-
state core is described in PSAR section 6.4.2 and evaluated in section 6.4.2 of this SE. PSAR
section 1.1.4.1.2 lists the American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) standards used to
ensure requirements in the specification are met. These include ASTM standards for the
graphite feedstock to make sure it is nuclear-grade and additional standards on impurities and
other key parameters like compressive strength. Testing on wear rate will also be performed to

                    OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION
                    OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION


confirm that the pebbles will not break down as they travel through the core. The fuel handling
system, described in PSAR section 7.3.6 also has the capability to remove damaged pebbles
from circulation.

The startup source is used in the 1/M approach to critical, as described in PSAR section 6.4.2.
PSAR section 3.10.7 provides a preliminary analysis of postulated radiological release from the
startup source assumes that it is a Cf-252 source with a strength of 400 mCi. Final selection of
the type and strength of the startup source as well as placement will be provided at the OL
stage. The NRC staff finds the basis for classification of the SFFPs and startup source as NST
acceptable for the CP based on the current safety analysis documented in PSAR chapter 3.

The chemical injection subsystem (CDCI) within the CDFS which is used to provide chemicals
needed for corrosion protection and scale build-up prevention to the condensate, feedwater,
and steam systems will be part of implementing the secondary water chemistry objectives of the
chemistry program, described in PSAR section 8.8.2. Ensuring this function is performed
through applying the chemistry program to steam generators, turbine, and feedwater system.

The HSCW provides cooling to various nuclear island SSCs and CICW provides cooling for the
CDFW, CDS, MS, and TG. While these systems do not currently and are not expected to
perform a function that mitigates an event, they may contribute to the frequency of various
initiating events such as loss of feedwater. The impact of these systems failing on the overall
facility risk will be assessed through the risk-significance evaluations described in the response
to RCI-1 dated August 14, 2026 (ML26230A155). The NRC staff finds the basis for the list of
secondary systems and components classified as NST acceptable for the CP based on the
current safety analysis documented in PSAR chapter 3.
The role of the ROST carts in the transport of spent and used fuel is described in PSAR section
7.3.1.1 through 7.3.1.3. As stated in PSAR section 7.3.1.3, spent fuel and used fuel storage
canisters are designed to survive falls from the ROST cart. Criticality safety analyses involving
various canister storage locations and configurations are documented in PSAR section 3.9 and
evaluated in section 3.9 of this SE. These analyses are sufficient to bound criticality safety
aspects related to the ROST cart for the CP. The NRC staff finds the basis for the classification
of the ROST carts as NST acceptable for the CP based on the current safety analysis
documented in PSAR chapter 3.
The MCR is located on the second floor of the controls and electrical building (CEB), which is
classified as NSRST and described in PSAR section 7.3.1.6. While the MCR is classified as
NST, the CEB is designed to protect operators and the NSRST SSCs in the CEB from eternal
hazards such as seismic, flooding, and tornado missiles. PSAR section 5.5.3 describes one
NSRST operator action required during some steam generator tube leak (SGTL) events to
identify the leaking bundle, isolate it, and restore active cooling through SSS with the intact
bundle. PSAR section 7.3.12 includes additional discussion on how this operator action is
performed using NSRST indications, displays, and human-machine interfaces in the distributed
control system (DCS). PSAR section 7.3.12 also states that the nuclear island HVAC system is
not required to support this operator action based on the timing of the event and the NIE
remains available to support the required DCS components because loss of both offsite and
backup power concurrent with an SGTL event is below the frequency cutoff for LBEs. The NRC

                    OFFICIAL USE ONLY – PROPRIETARY INFORMATION


staff finds this basis for classification of the MCR, MCR HVAC, and the NIE supporting this
function to be acceptable for the CP based on the current design and scope of LBEs.
The PMC provides operators with the capability to monitor the plant from outside the MCR,
consistent with the requirements of PDC 19 and provides radiation monitoring and seismic
monitoring through dedicated subsystems, consistent with the requirements of PDC 13. The
radiation monitoring system (RMS) provides instrumentation, monitoring, and alarms in fuel
storage and radioactive waste systems consistent with PDC 63 and provides airborne

Evaluation Under 10 CFR 50.34(a)(11) for Multiunit Sites
PSAR Section 1.4.5 indicates that the requirements under 10 CFR 50.34(a)(11) are not
applicable to the LMGS because LMGS is a single nuclear power plant with four reactor
modules and there are not existing or planned nuclear power plants co-located on the LMGS
site. The NRC staff agrees that 10 CFR 50.34(a)(11) is not applicable. Interactions and safety
considerations for sharing of systems between modules within the plant are assessed through
the evaluation of PDC 5 throughout chapter 6 and 7 of this SE.
